extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and practitioners preparing/submitting nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listings to the USPTO (and practitioners filing international or foreign applications involving sequence listings)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards for including nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences in a patent application's 'Sequence Listing' (format, content, identifiers, submission media, international differences, and fees). Intended to guide preparation and submission so the Sequence Listing complies with 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 (and related WIPO/PCT rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length thresholds for applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence rules apply to unbranched sequences of four or more amino acids or ten or more nucleotides (sequences with fewer than ten specifically defined nucleotides or four specifically defined amino acids are excluded). 'Specifically defined' excludes placeholder symbols (e.g., 'Xaa' for amino acids, 'n' for nucleotides) as defined in the CFR appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Branched sequences are specifically excluded. The 4-amino-acid threshold aligns with industry database practices; the 10-nucleotide threshold is intended to encompass sequences to which the smallest probe will bind stably. Situations where applicability is borderline are resolved case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted/reserved symbols and representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide and amino acid sequences must be representable using the symbols set forth in 37 CFR 1.822 and the relevant appendices (Appendices A–F to 37 CFR part 1, Subpart G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nucleotide sequences are limited to the allowed symbols in the rules; unusual phosphate linkages (e.g., certain natural end caps) do not render the rules inapplicable. Amino acid sequences are limited to the L-amino acids commonly found in nature; presence of D-amino acids excludes the sequence from the rules (but voluntary compliance is encouraged using 'Xaa'). Modified linkages, cross-links, end caps, and non-peptidyl bonds should be described in the Features section if needed. The rules are not intended to encompass unrelated subject matter (e.g., synthetic resins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of sequences disclosed in application text
rubrics_metrics.description: All sequences meeting the length thresholds that are disclosed in the application (whether claimed or not) must be included in the Sequence Listing if they are presented as a string of nucleotide bases or amino acids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sequence is only referred to by name plus a publication or accession reference, it need not be included unless it is 'essential material' (see MPEP § 608.01(p)). The Office's goal is a comprehensive database, so disclosed strings must be listed even if applicant considers them prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of sequence variants
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary sequence may be presented and variants (e.g., conservatively modified variants, truncations) discussed without listing every variant separately, provided the primary sequence is listed and variants are properly annotated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a variant meeting length thresholds is disclosed by enumeration anywhere in the application, it must be presented in the Sequence Listing. Examples: 'conservatively modified variants thereof' can be used; implied C-terminal deletions (e.g., deletion of 1–5 residues) need not all be separately listed but should be annotated. Sequences considered essential to understanding or claimed should be included as separate entries. The Office database will only contain the unmodified (listed) sequence, so clear annotation is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence identifier requirement (SEQ ID NO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disclosed nucleic acid and/or amino acid sequence must appear separately in the Sequence Listing and be assigned a sequence identifier (e.g., 'SEQ ID NO:'), with identifiers beginning at 1 and increasing sequentially by integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of variants of the label (e.g., 'SEQ NO.', 'Seq. Id. No.') is acceptable if it is clear. Sequence identifiers should, where practical, reflect the order in which sequences are discussed in the application. When text or claims discuss a sequence that is set forth in the Sequence Listing, the sequence identifier must be referenced at all occurrences (even if the sequence is enumerated in the text). Fragments (e.g., 'residues 14 to 243 of SEQ ID NO:23') are permissible without separately presenting the fragment in the Sequence Listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive conformance to sequence rules (single format requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications that fall within the definition of sequences under 37 CFR 1.821(a), applicants must conform exclusively to the presentation and description requirements of 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 to avoid multiple conflicting sequence formats in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimizes confusion from multiple formats. Although sequences should not be duplicated in the Sequence Listing and drawings per 37 CFR 1.83(a), drawings may be used to depict features not representable in the Sequence Listing (e.g., double-stranded nucleotides, sticky ends, homology diagrams); sequences shown in drawings must still be included in the Sequence Listing and identified by SEQ ID NO either in the drawing or in the Brief Description of the Drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing as a separate part of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing must be submitted as a separate part of the specification using the format and symbols in 37 CFR 1.822 and 1.823.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable submission forms: (1) ASCII plain text file via the USPTO patent electronic filing system; (2) PDF image file submitted via the USPTO electronic filing system; or (3) physical sheets of paper. If submitted as PDF or paper, an accompanying CRF (computer readable form) text file per 37 CFR 1.824 must also be provided. The listing submitted as a separate part of the specification must begin on a new page when provided as PDF or paper. For ASCII submissions via EFS, an incorporation-by-reference paragraph in the specification is required (name of file, date of creation, size in bytes) in applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) unless exceptions apply (e.g., international applications meeting PCT Rule 5.2(a) or national stage where listing was previously communicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII plain text EFS submission specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting the Sequence Listing as an ASCII plain text file via the USPTO electronic filing system, the file must be ASCII plain text with a '.txt' extension and must not be compressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ASCII plain text file submitted via EFS will serve as both the Sequence Listing (37 CFR 1.821(c)) and the CRF (37 CFR 1.821(e)) for applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, eliminating the need for PDF/paper duplicates. Applicants should include an incorporation-by-reference statement in the specification identifying the text file (except where not required). Checker software (Checker4) is available on the USPTO website to verify certain compliance aspects; consult its User Notes for scope of verifiable errors. Do not submit a second copy of the listing if the ASCII file is submitted via EFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: File size limits and required media
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO electronic filing system accepts Sequence Listing and CRF text files up to 100 megabytes; text files larger than 100 MB must be submitted on read-only optical disc(s) per 37 CFR 1.52(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using read-only optical discs, ASCII files may be compressed and can be split across multiple discs if necessary (follow labeling rules). If an ASCII plain text file is submitted on read-only optical disc(s), the specification must contain an incorporation-by-reference paragraph identifying the file name, creation date, and size (except where exceptions apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Large (mega) Sequence Listing fees and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Sequence Listing ASCII plain text file of 300 MB or more is subject to a fee under 37 CFR 1.21(o) (two tiers: Tier 1 for 300–800 MB, Tier 2 for >800 MB). The fee is due upon the first submission that exceeds the applicable threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee encourages omission of non-essential sequence data to reduce Office burden. The fee does not apply during the international phase of an international application but does apply to national stage submissions under 35 U.S.C. 371, including submissions pursuant to PCT Article 20. If a later submission increases the file size into a higher tier, the difference is due at that time. Subsequent reductions in size do not refund prior fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc labeling and copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting Sequence Listings on read-only optical disc(s), discs must be labeled 'Copy 1' and 'Copy 2' (duplicate copy) and include a statement that the copies are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the two discs are not identical, the Office will use the disc labeled 'Copy 1' for processing. Compressed ASCII plain text files that do not fit on a single disc may be split into multiple parts and must be labeled per 37 CFR 1.52(e)(5)(vi) and 1.824(b)(2)(iv). Large tables (>50 pages) may be included on the disc under certain rules (see 1.52(e)(1)(iii) and 1.58 provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT/WIPO) sequence listing harmonization points
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants filing international applications or in countries adhering to WIPO ST.25 (2009) should follow additional/overlapping requirements: numeric identifier <221> must use selections from Tables 5 and 6 of WIPO ST.25, and ST.25 paragraph 24 requires a blank line between numeric identifiers when certain digits change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free text in numeric identifier <223> in the Sequence Listing must be repeated in the main part of the description in the language of the application (PCT Rule 5.2(b)); it is recommended to place such free text in a 'Sequence Listing Free Text' section. Sequence listings filed after the international filing date are generally not considered part of the disclosure (see PCT Article 34, Rules 26 and 91 exceptions). WIPO ST.25 paragraph 4(v) requires an accompanying statement with the specific wording: 'the information recorded in electronic form furnished under PCT Rule 13ter is identical to the sequence listing as contained in the international application.' Software (PatentIn v3.5.1) generates ST.25-compliant listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: When sequences appear only in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a sequence is presented in a drawing figure (to show double-stranded features, sticky ends, homology, epitopes, domains, etc.), the sequence must still be included in the Sequence Listing if it meets 37 CFR 1.821(a) and must be identified by sequence identifier in the drawing or Brief Description of the Drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequences should not be duplicated between the Sequence Listing and the drawings per 37 CFR 1.83(a), but drawings are appropriate when certain features cannot be represented in the Sequence Listing. The Sequence Listing remains the definitive machine-readable disclosure for Office databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of sequence identifiers on statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sequence identifiers (e.g., SEQ ID NO:X) is a shorthand for referring to sequences and does not alter the substantive disclosure or claiming requirements under 35 U.S.C. 112 (a) or (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including SEQ ID NO references does not restrict how an invention can be claimed and should not raise 35 U.S.C. 112 issues by itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRF submission requirements when not using ASCII EFS file
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Sequence Listing is submitted as a PDF image file or on physical paper sheets, a separate CRF in accordance with 37 CFR 1.824 must also be submitted (either via EFS or on read-only optical disc) per 37 CFR 1.821(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national stage entries under 35 U.S.C. 371 and international applications being searched/examined by the US ISA/IPEA, a CRF per 1.824 is required if an ASCII plain text listing compliant with 1.824 has not been submitted. The ASCII plain text file and CRF must be a single file when submitted electronically; do not submit compressed CRF files when using EFS (follow 1.824 compression/disc rules when using optical discs).
